steps.tx: The hallmark **Dupuytren contracture** is a benign, progressive fibroproliferative disorder of the palmar and digital fascia, characterised by pathognomonic conversion of normal fascial bands into diseased, contracting cords. It predominantly affects northern European males over 50 years of age, strongly associated with HLA-DRB1*15 and positive family history.
steps.say: Dupuytren disease turns the normal bands of the palm into thick contracting cords that drag the fingers bent. It picks out men over fifty of northern European ancestry, runs in families with the HLA-DRB1 fifteen marker, and marches slowly from a small pit to a hand that cannot open.

nodes.label: TGF-beta1 release and fibroblast differentiation into myofibroblasts
Type III collagen deposition and irreversible fascial contracture

steps.tx: The key cellular mediator driving fascial contracture is the **myofibroblast**, expressing alpha-smooth muscle actin. Cellular proliferation produces an abnormal extracellular matrix characterized by an inverted collagen ratio, where embryonic **type III collagen** increases markedly relative to mature normal type I collagen.
steps.say: The engine of the contracture is the myofibroblast, a fibroblast armed with smooth muscle actin that pulls like a muscle cell. As these cells multiply they flood the fascia with embryonic type three collagen instead of mature type one, flipping the normal ratio and building a cord that shortens.

steps.tx: Ectopic fibromatosis manifestations in Dupuytren diathesis include plantar fibromatosis known as **Ledderhose disease**, penile fibromatosis causing chordee curvature known as **Peyronie disease**, and fibrous knuckle pads over the dorsal proximal interphalangeal joints termed Garrod pads that occur frequently in severe clinical phenotypes.
steps.say: Dupuytren diathesis means the same fibromatosis erupting elsewhere. Lumps in the soles are Ledderhose disease, a bent penis is Peyronie disease, and firm pads over the finger knuckles are Garrod pads, and a patient carrying these extras almost always grows a fiercer and earlier contracture.

steps.tx: The anatomy of diseased cords dictates digital deformity patterns. The pretendinous band forms the pretendinous cord causing metacarpophalangeal contracture. The spiral cord, arising from pretendinous band, spiral band, Grayson ligament, and lateral digital sheet, displaces the **neurovascular bundle** midline, superficial, and proximal.
steps.say: Each cord bends its own joint, so learn the anatomy before cutting. The pretendinous cord runs down the palm and flexes the knuckle joint, while the spiral cord wraps around the finger and drags the nerve and artery toward the midline and up to the surface, exactly where a careless blade would find them.

nodes.label: Pretendinous band + spiral band + Grayson ligament + lateral sheet
Neurovascular bundle displaced superficial and toward the midline

steps.tx: Clinical assessment utilizes the **Hueston tabletop test**: the patient is asked to place their hand flat on a table. Inability to place the palm completely flat confirms fixed flexion contracture. Standard indications for surgical fasciectomy include MCP joint flexion contracture exceeding 30 degrees or any PIP joint flexion contracture.
steps.say: Test the hand on a tabletop: a palm that cannot lie flat has a fixed contracture, which is the Hueston test. Offer fasciectomy once the knuckle bends more than thirty degrees, but do not wait at the middle joint, where any fixed bend at all earns an operation.

right.title: PIP Joint Contracture
points: Involves check-rein ligaments and volar plate

steps.tx: Limited or selective **fasciectomy** is the standard surgical procedure, excising only macroscopic diseased fascial cords while sparing normal fascia. Bruner zig-zag incisions or longitudinal incisions combined with multiple Z-plasties prevent longitudinal linear scar contractures and provide wide exposure of the displaced neurovascular bundles.
steps.say: Limited fasciectomy removes only the visible diseased cords and leaves healthy fascia behind. Open the finger with Bruner zig-zag cuts or lengthen a straight cut with Z-plasties, because a straight scar would contract into a new bend, and expect the nerve bundles to sit displaced until you find them.

steps.tx: The **McCash open-palm technique** leaves transverse palmar skin incisions unstitched to heal by secondary intention. This method virtually eliminates postoperative palmar hematoma formation, reduces pain, and allows immediate active finger mobilization, with full epithelialization achieved in 3 to 5 weeks.
steps.say: McCash taught a counterintuitive trick for the palm: leave the transverse wound open. An open palm cannot trap a haematoma, hurts less, and lets the fingers move from day one, with the raw area skinning over by itself in three to five weeks.

steps.tx: Non-surgical alternatives include needle fasciotomy and enzymatic cordolysis using **collagenase Clostridium histolyticum**. Collagenase degrades type I and type III collagen, followed by finger extension manipulation 24 to 72 hours later. Complications include skin tears, local hematoma, and rare flexor tendon rupture.
steps.say: Not every cord needs a knife. A needle can divide it through the skin, or injected collagenase can dissolve the type one and three collagen so the finger can be straightened one to three days later. Warn of skin splits and bruising, and of the rare but real ruptured flexor tendon.
